correctness.rationale: The exact finite domain consists of all 4096 initial binary states on each of 19 explicit graphs. Verified that two standard-library programs, with distinct Frucht graph constructions, distinct majority-update implementations and distinct enumeration strategies, agree on all 19 complete rows including gains/losses, first-entry histograms, recurrent period-one and period-two counts. Every cyclic component is verified length 1 or 2; longest first entry 8, achieved. The tie/self-substitution lemma follows from the median-of-three Boolean identity. No inference from finite samples to a larger domain is made.

evidence: Kaaser–Mallmann-Trenn–Natale (2015) prove general voting-time bounds and NP-hardness, not exact Frucht time or unanimity-basin sizes.
Benjamini–Chan–O'Donnell–Tamuz–Tan (2014) study majority dynamics and random-graph consensus, not all single-edge deletions of a fixed asymmetric cubic graph.
The classical Goles–Olivos period-two theorem, quoted in both sources, forces eventual periods at most two but supplies no edge-resolved attraction populations.
broader_coverage.reasoning: General period and upper-bound theorems encompass the rule and graphs but do not imply numerical gains/losses, signed response or a sharp eight-update cutoff for these explicit 19 maps. A covering general formula was not found; this is a scope-based implication comparison, not proof that no such formula exists.

value.rationale: Every one of the 18 structurally inequivalent edges of a canonical 12-vertex asymmetric cubic network is analyzed, giving a natural complete finite invariant and a nontrivial two-sided sensitivity statement: each deletion both creates and destroys some consensus-attaining initial conditions, while the net sign splits 11 positive and 7 negative. The five sharp eight-update defects and full entry census quantify a distinct dynamical cost. The complete gain/loss rather than a one-off numerical example is motivated by non-monotonicity of consensus under local bond changes.
